function: Fall detection (human activity sensing): the learned ST-GNN is a binary fall/no-fall classifier of RSS from passive RFID tags (p. 7); not one of the seven areas (function).
notes: Reason function (first applicable code; it is a research article with a learned component acting on physical RSS measurements, not above the PHY). The only learned component, the ST-GNN (GAT + GRU + temporal attention, supervised with cross-entropy), detects falls from measured RFID RSS: p. 6: "the ST-GNN is a machine learning-based approach, using graph neural networks to model the spatio-temporal relationships of RSS variations, which is more accurate and robust for fall detection"; p. 7: "Fall detection output layer is a binary classifier, identifying whether a fall event has occurred". This is human activity sensing, not the design of beams, waveforms, or resources that serve sensing and communication (area 5), nor any other area. The communication side is RSS-based secret key generation between the two reader antennas (p. 2: "key generation ensuring resilient and secure communication between the two receive antennas"), done without learning by threshold peak detection (p. 4: "We propose a time-series-peak-pattern approach for key generation between two users"; p. 5: "Only peaks that exceed Ht are considered valid for bit generation"), a physical-layer security function also outside the seven areas. Title and DOI 10.1109/TCCN.2025.3573413 confirmed on p. 1.
